_readme: Every tunable value for one demo video. This is the ONLY file an agent edits
for a parameter change — never the generated timing/storyboard artifact, which
is routinely 50-100 KB and costs thousands of tokens to read.
The build step projects these values into the renderer's own format.
Before changing anything here, check the cost table in SKILL.md: only the
'audio' block is cheap to change. Everything else forces a full re-render, so
batch those changes and render once.
Defaults below are the validated values from the reference implementation.

project.name: my-demo
project.title: Human-readable title shown on the title card
project.lede: One-line summary shown under the storyboard heading.
project.objective: Viewer will be able to <action verb> <what>.
project.audience: Who is watching, and what they already know.
project.callToAction: What the viewer should do next.
project._objectiveNote: Use an action verb — configure, explain, compare, decide. Defining this before scripting is established instructional-design sequencing, and it is what disciplines `framing` from being merely a tone.
project._framingNote: celebratory = lead with wins, don't dwell on gaps. balanced = name limitations too. Changes wording throughout, not just tone.
project._emphasisNote: decisions | mechanics | impact — these produce very different scripts.
project._noGoNote: Topics, names, or figures that must not appear.
project.seriesNote: If part of a series, keep voice/timing/audio identical across parts unless deliberately varied — mismatched loudness is obvious on back-to-back playback.
project._playbackNote: back-to-back = don't retread the earlier part. standalone = re-establish context. both = soften the opening.
project._preTrainingNote: Terms/components an earlier part already established, which this video may assume. Null = assume nothing.

accessibility._note: Planning-time constraints, not post-production additions. See references/planning.md §3.
accessibility._narrationNote: REQUIRED before render. This pipeline has one audio track, so narration doubles as audio description (WCAG G226). Confirm every meaningful diagram, UI state change, and on-screen text is named in narration. Never 'this' or 'here' — name the actual label.
accessibility._colorNote: Diffs, state indicators, and highlights need a second channel — glyph, shape, label, or narration (WCAG 1.4.1).
accessibility._contrastNote: 4.5:1 normal text, 3:1 large text and diagram elements. Includes the code theme in any screen recording.
accessibility._flashingNote: No more than 3 flashes in any 1s period, including decorative transitions (WCAG 2.3.1).

narration._pronunciationsNote: Map term -> how it should be read, e.g. {"KQL": "K Q L", "Kusto": "KOO-stoh"}. Build this as a planning artifact. TTS will not improvise correctly the way a voice actor would.
narration.numbersConvention: Write numbers as they should be spoken.
narration._numbersNote: Versions, dates, percentages, currency. The most common cause of an otherwise-perfect render needing a redo.

downstream._reuseNote: Will this material also become slides or a doc? If so, as what MODE? Per Diátaxis a tutorial walkthrough and a reference doc serve different needs — video is not a lossless source for documentation.

signOff._note: Who must approve the script and final cut. Distinct from the render approval gate, which is about spending render time; this is about who owns the content being correct.

voice.name: en-US-AndrewNeural
voice._tierNote: neural | legacy. Engine tier matters more than identity-matching across a series: a modern neural voice is materially better than a legacy one, and that gap is larger than the cost of an inconsistent-but-good voice between parts.
voice._note: Changing engine, name, or speed invalidates every downstream duration. Expensive.

timing._wpsNote: Effective speech rate for the word-budget check in validate-timing. Measure it from a real render and record it here (or in calibration-observed.json, which wins). This is calibration data, not logic — it was the ONLY divergence between project copies of that script.
timing._note: perceivedGap is what a viewer HEARS: tail(clip N) + inserted silence + head(clip N+1). It is not the length of the inserted file. See bug-ledger entry 6.
timing._overridesNote: Map of segmentId -> ms, e.g. {"origin": 4000} to hold a longer beat after one segment. Leave empty for uniform gaps. Treat as optional everywhere — see bug-ledger entry 8.

audio._note: THE CHEAP BLOCK. Changes here swap the audio track and reuse the video stream byte-for-byte. Minutes, not tens of minutes.

music._presetNote: Named bed in make-music.mjs: 'warm' (I-V-ii-IV in F, settled) or 'bright' (vi-IV-I-V in G, more movement). Sibling videos in a series should use DIFFERENT presets — related, not a repeat. Add a new preset rather than editing one, so rendered videos keep their bed.
music._note: Generated rather than sampled, so there is no licensing to clear.

levels._note: Music lifting ~6 dB in the gaps turns tuned silence into something deliberate. Keep narration level identical across a series.

fades._note: fades.inMs MUST be shorter than timing.leadInMs or the bed arrives under the narration. See bug-ledger entry 4.

limiter._note: MUST stay false. ffmpeg alimiter defaults to level=true and will gain-ride the entire mix, silently undoing every adjustment. See bug-ledger entry 1.

preview._note: Draft settings for the approval gate. Declared here so they are not reinvented each session. Scale is the biggest lever — 0.5 roughly halves render time.

render._note: estimatedFullRenderMinutes is FOR A VIDEO OF estimatedForVideoLength — roughly 9-10x runtime in the reference implementation. Scale it to the video actually being rendered, and quote it when asking for render approval.
render._previewNote: Set previewSegment to a segment id to render just that one before committing to a full pass.
render._measureNote: Replace both estimates from the first real run on this machine. The defaults are from the reference implementation's hardware, not yours.
